submissions.title: Lexington council extends data center ban
submissions.excerpt: set a noise limit of 30 decibels and cap energy use at 25 megawatts
submissions.suggestedProjectName: DartPoints Lexington (former Lexmark Data Center), Fayette County, KY
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: Lexington-Fayette Urban County Council voted unanimously on 2026-10-07 to extend the citywide data-center moratorium (previously set to expire Oct. 31, 2026) to October 2027, and separately adopted a zoning text amendment (ZOTA, passed 2026-10-13 per a follow-up Spectrum News piece) capping new data-center electricity use at 25 MW, a 30 dB noise limit at the property line, and a ban on facilities over 50,000 sq ft. This directly affects the DartPoints campus (the former Lexmark Data Center), which had sought 50 MW — the stated trigger for the moratorium. submissions.title: Mayor Lurie signs San Francisco data center moratorium
submissions.excerpt: a 45-day moratorium on data centers that would pause city approvals of the facilities
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie signed a 45-day citywide moratorium on new data-center approvals on Friday 2026-10-16 (effective immediately regardless of signature, per the ordinance), after the Board of Supervisors passed it unanimously the week before (first reported 2026-10-06, authored by Supervisor Shamann Walton). It directs the Planning Department to study energy/water/air impacts and can reportedly be extended up to ~22 months. No specific project is named in coverage, so this is submitted as a jurisdiction-wide restriction rather than linked to a projectId. CAVEAT: same WebFetch outage as the Lexington submission above — excerpt reconstructed from search snippets, not a direct article fetch; please verify exact wording against the primary link. Secondary sourcing (local news), not a primary ordinance-text link.
